tables.title: Conflicts and inconsistencies between sources — Item

rows.label: Divestiture proceeds appear on three bases: "net proceeds of approximately $900 million" (EX-99.1 May page:4, an estimate at closing), "net cash proceeds of $888 million received" (10-Q Q3 page:56, cash received in the nine months), and "$894 million after final purchase price adjustments" (10-Q Q3 page:13, final, with part settled after September 30, 2026).
The same figure of $894 million is also the principal of 2028 Civitas notes repurchased in the tender ("we repurchased $894 million aggregate principal amount", 10-Q Q3 page:20).
The divestiture is named "South Texas Divestiture" in the 10-Qs and "Galvan Divestiture" in a footnote to the November release guidance table, dated the same day ("the Galvan Divestiture").

Covenant level: 10-K states a total funded debt to adjusted EBITDAX ceiling and a current ratio floor; the Fourth Amendment (January 30, 2026) made "certain other amendments to the financial covenant definitions".
Gain on divestiture: Q2 shows "an estimated gain of $262 million" (10-Q Q3 page:37), the nine-month figure is "(260)" with a third-quarter loss of "2" (10-Q Q3 page:60).

Credit agreement, Fourth Amendment, indentures and supplemental indentures are not supplied. The 10-K exhibit list names them (page:201 "Fourth Amendment to Seventh Amended and Restated Credit Agreement"; page:200 "First Supplemental Indenture, dated as of January 30, 2026") but the executed documents are not in the pack, and the context sets legal_documents to none.

Current financial covenant levels. Only the 10-K states them, before the amendment that changed the definitions. The quarterly report states compliance and the test but not the level or the reported ratio.

Revolver maturity detail. The Fourth Amendment extends maturity "for elected revolving commitments to January 30, 2031"; the maturity of non-elected commitments is not stated, and whether the springing maturity added by the Third Amendment (10-K page:158) still applies is not stated.

Guarantors and obligors by instrument. The filing says notes are guaranteed by "each of our existing subsidiaries that guarantee the Credit Agreement" (10-Q Q3 page:21) without naming them; the context lists no guarantors. Restricted versus unrestricted subsidiaries are not described.
Credit ratings are not supplied. The 10-Q Q3 (page:51) says two agencies upgraded the company but names neither agency nor the level; the context ratings list is empty.

Investor slides. The November release (page:1) refers to "accompanying slides" at the company website; the pack holds earnings releases only, no presentation. No slide, image or speaker note is claimed as inspected.
Reserves after the merger. The only reserve and standardized measure disclosures are year-end FY2025 (10-K pages:21-24, 187-190), covering the company before the merger; the 10-Qs do not update them.
Purchase price allocation is preliminary (10-Q Q3 page:11 "The purchase price allocation for the Merger is preliminary"), so acquired-asset and assumed-liability amounts may change.
Pro forma leverage or EBITDAX including Civitas before January 30, 2026 is not supplied; only pro forma revenue and net income are (10-Q Q3 page:13). Prior-year columns are the pre-merger company.

Discrete quarter and cash-flow detail. Cash flows, cash interest and cash taxes are year-to-date in each 10-Q; discrete quarters need subtraction of consecutive filings. The Q1 and Q2 10-Q statements were checked in this review only for period identity, the covenant sentence and the cover; their line items were not read here.

Off-balance-sheet and non-debt claims. Delivery commitments, a drilling commitment and liquidated damages are described in 10-Q Q3 page:22. Pension and lease detail is last given at year-end in the 10-K (pages:176, 180). The 10-Q describes no pension or lease change.

Extraction fidelity. Tables are flattened to text lines, so a dash cell can shift columns (for example premium cells on 10-Q Q3 page:19). No fidelity review against the original HTML was done; successful extraction is not a fidelity review.
Currency and units: the sources print USD in millions, with some sentences in billions. No other currency or period basis was found; the context currency and periods match the sources.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: SM Energy is an independent oil and gas producer whose profile changed in one step on 2026-01-30, when it acquired Civitas Resources for stock and became a four-basin operator, then partly reversed the change by selling its southern Maverick Basin assets on 2026-04-30. For a creditor the transaction matters for four reasons. First, it was paid mainly in equity, with no sponsor and no leveraged buyout structure; the debt increase came from assumed notes, not new borrowing, and the revolver was left undrawn. Second, management used asset-sale proceeds and cash flow to retire the shortest notes and part of the highest-coupon assumed issue, so the first note maturity is mid-2028 and revolver availability is intact. Third, the operating base is oil-weighted and exposed to price, basis and takeaway constraints, partly offset by a hedge book priced below recent realized oil prices that shows as a liability. Fourth, the evidence on ownership control, legal capacity under the indentures and reserves after the merger is missing, so conclusions about willingness are supported by documented actions only, and conclusions about permissions are not drawn. The documented behaviour is deleveraging with continuing shareholder returns; no priming, uptiering, drop-down, debt-funded distribution or related-party leakage appears in the supplied text.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On 2025-11-02 SM Energy signed a merger agreement with Civitas Resources, Inc. (10-K page:14). Stockholders approved the share issuance on 2026-01-27 and the merger closed on 2026-01-30 (Q3 page:33). Each Civitas share was converted into 1.45 SM Energy shares; 124 million shares were issued, equal to 52 percent of the enlarged share count, valued at 2.4 billion on the closing price. The purchase accounting (preliminary) shows equity consideration of 2,409, replacement awards of 29, cash of 226 and total consideration of 2,664 (Q3 page:11); the cash included 201 to repay the Civitas revolver, which released its liens, and 25 for an employee retention program (Q3 page:12). SM Energy is the accounting acquirer, the deal was a tax-free reorganization, and 18 of transaction costs were expensed in the nine months (Q3 page:10). The company assumed 4.9 billion principal of Civitas unsecured senior notes (Q3 page:18); the purchase price allocation lists senior notes assumed at a fair value of 5,090 (Q3 page:11). The Fourth Amendment to the credit agreement, signed at closing, added the Civitas subsidiaries as guarantors, extended the maturity of elected commitments to 2031-01-30, raised commitments from 2.0 billion to 2.5 billion and the borrowing base from 3.0 billion to 5.0 billion, and amended financial covenant definitions (Q3 page:17). Management reports that it actioned about 400 million of run-rate synergies against an original 200 million target (R3 page:1); this is Management Language and no synergy realization in the cash flow statement is supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The divestiture and the debt actions that followed form the second leg. On 2026-02-17 SM Energy agreed to sell about 61,000 net acres in its southern Maverick Basin for 950 million of cash, with a deposit of 7.5 percent placed in escrow (10-K page:183). The sale closed on 2026-04-30 and, after a post-quarter settlement, total net cash proceeds were 894 with a gain of 260 (Q3 page:13). New debt issued in 2026: 1.0 billion of 6.625 percent Senior Notes due 2034, issued at par on 2026-03-09, with net proceeds of 984 after fees (Q3 page:20), used to fund a tender offer. The tender repurchased 894 principal of the 8.375 percent notes due 2028, at 103.175 percent of principal, for total consideration of 924, leaving 456 outstanding (Q3 page:20). Proceeds of the sale redeemed at par the 400 of 5.0 percent notes due 2026 on 2026-05-11 and the 419 of 6.75 percent notes due 2026 on 2026-06-01, and cash flow redeemed the 417 of 6.625 percent notes due 2027 on 2026-09-04 (Q3 pages:20-21). There was no new issuance after the 2034 notes in the supplied sources, and the revolver was undrawn at each quarter end. Net debt fell from 7,353 at 2026-03-31 to 6,014 at 2026-09-30 as stated in the CP-1 handoff, and management says it is on track for low one-times leverage at mid-cycle prices by year-end 2026 (R3 page:2, Management Language; the term is not defined in the sources).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability and margin risk. Evidence: oil is the dominant revenue line (Q3 page:14) and gas realizations fell to 0.17 per Mcf in Q2 on regional differentials (Q3 page:40). Mechanic: price-taking producer with partial hedges; swap and collar floors are below Q3 realized oil prices, so settlements reduce cash now, while the hedge book still limits downside. Implication: cash flow and leverage move with oil and basis; a fall in prices would be cushioned for 2026 and 2027 by hedge volumes (Q3 page:24), but the volumes against 2027 production are not determinable because 2027 production guidance is not supplied. Counter-evidence: the hedge liability and conflicts logged below. 2. Merger and integration. Evidence: 124 million shares issued; 4.9 billion of notes assumed; synergy claims are Management Language (R3 page:1). Mechanic: scale gain and cost take-out against integration cost, unmet drilling commitment and operational downtime on acquired assets (R3 page:2). Implication: the combined entity carries more debt than the standalone company, but the sources show the debt falling and liquidity intact; integration cost and execution risk remain through 2026. 3. Refinancing and maturity. Evidence: no notes mature until mid-2028 (Q3 page:21). Mechanic: the shortest notes were retired from sale proceeds and cash flow, and high-coupon assumed debt was partly replaced with a lower-coupon issue. Implication: refinancing risk and interest burden are reduced for the next two years; the 2028 maturities and 2030-2033 high-coupon notes remain the next negotiation points. 4. Sponsor alignment and distributions. Evidence: widely held listed equity, no sponsor, equity-paid deal. Mechanic: shareholder returns are funded from free cash flow beside debt reduction. Implication: no extraction pattern is documented; the monitoring point is the pace of buybacks against leverage targets, because management states returns are evaluated "in the context of our leverage trajectory" (Q3 page:64). 5. Key uncertainties. Reserve base after the merger and sale; customer concentration after the merger; current covenant terms; ratings; legal capacity. Implication: these block analysis of asset coverage and permitted distributions, and are logged as gaps, not as adverse conclusions.

rows.label: SM Energy is a widely held, oil-weighted US shale producer that expanded to four basins through the January 2026 Civitas merger, then sold assets and redeemed notes to cut debt. No creditor-adverse behaviour is documented.
The merger was paid in shares, and former Civitas holders own 52 percent of the company; no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed.
Asset sales and cash flow retired notes due 2026 and 2027 and part of a high-coupon 2028 issue, leaving no note maturity until mid-2028.
Revenue is mostly oil, and the Permian Basin supplies about half of production revenue. Hedge prices sit below recent realized oil prices, and the derivative position is a liability.
Shareholder returns continue beside debt reduction: dividends and buybacks are paid and a buyback target is set as a share of free cash flow.
Reserves, customer concentration and employee data are from before the merger and the asset sale.
Prior ownership and dividend recapitalisation history

Transparent reporting: recurring non-GAAP reconciliations, covenant compliance statements and subsequent-event disclosure

Investor slides and the call presentation referenced in the releases (R3 page:4)

Synergy realization in reported results; integration cost beyond the reconciliation lines

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: SM Energy's credit standing is sound and improving, but it depends on oil prices and on a newly merged earnings base. The strongest support is balance-sheet strength: net debt of USD 6,014 million is 1.42x trailing adjusted EBITDAX, the revolver is undrawn, liquidity is USD 2,940 million, and no note matures before mid-2028. The weakest point is that trailing earnings blend the old and merged company, so leverage is not on a clean pro forma basis, and covenant terms, ratings and legal documents are not in the sources. The outcome will be decided by oil prices and basis through 2027, by whether free cash flow keeps funding both debt reduction and shareholder returns, and by how the USD 3,956 million of notes due 2028 to 2031 is managed.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: SM Energy cut net debt by USD 1,339 million in two quarters, from USD 7,353 million at 2026-03-31 to USD 6,014 million at 2026-09-30, and trailing leverage fell from 2.79x to 1.42x over the same dates [CP-1: leverage and net debt tables; calculation 3]. The mechanism was asset-sale proceeds of USD 894 million and operating cash flow, which together redeemed the 2026 and 2027 notes at par while the revolver stayed undrawn at each quarter end [CP-1A: transaction summary]. The ratio improved partly because trailing earnings gradually absorbed more of the acquired business, so some of the decline is a perimeter effect and not debt repayment alone. The Civitas merger closed on 2026-01-30 and was equity-funded, so SM Energy's creditors face a larger company with the same unsecured senior notes and a secured revolver, not a leveraged buyout.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is strong: cash of USD 442 million plus USD 2,498 million of undrawn revolver capacity gives USD 2,940 million, while the borrowing base of USD 5,000 million is twice the USD 2,500 million of commitments, so availability is capped by lender commitments, not by reserves [CP-1: liquidity]. The maturity ladder is USD 856 million in 2028, USD 750 million in 2029, USD 1,000 million in 2030, USD 1,350 million in 2031 and USD 2,500 million across 2032 to 2034, so the wall begins in mid-2028 and totals USD 3,956 million across 2028 to 2031 [CP-1: debt maturities]. Cash generation covers the dividends: operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 845 million in the nine months against USD 187 million of dividends and USD 166 million of share repurchases, leaving USD 492 million before asset-sale proceeds [CP-1: calculation 7; this module's calculation 4].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The cost of the debt stack is the main structural concern. The notes carry a weighted coupon of 7.90 percent, or USD 510.1 million of coupons a year, and the notes assumed from Civitas, USD 3,556 million at 8.375 to 9.625 percent, are the most expensive layer, with a weighted coupon of 8.85 percent [CP-1: debt schedule; calculation 2]. Trailing cash interest cover of 12.73x blends the lighter pre-merger interest burden with the post-merger burden; against run-rate coupons the cover is 8.28x, which is the better guide to the current stack. Whether the high-coupon notes can be called or refinanced early depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings carry commodity risk. Oil was about 84 percent of Q3 2026 production revenue and the Permian Basin about half of it [CP-1A: company and operating model]. Hedges are swaps and collars through the second quarter of 2028 with prices below recent realized oil prices, so they cost cash now and cap upside, and the net derivative position is a liability of USD 460 million [CP-1A: hedging]. Operating issues also matter: oil production guidance was cut for Permian downtime on acquired assets and Uinta takeaway constraints, and lease operating cost per barrel of oil equivalent has risen every quarter since Q4 2025 [CP-1A: volume risks, cost structure]. Claims outside the debt figure include delivery commitments with up to USD 205 million of deficiency payments if nothing were delivered, liquidated damages of up to USD 64 million under a drilling agreement, and a drilling commitment management expects to be excused [CP-1: claims outside the debt figure].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. SM Energy has low net leverage of 1.42x on the filed trailing basis and has shown it will use asset sales and cash flow to retire debt, with USD 1,236 million of notes redeemed at par since March from sale proceeds and cash flow (400, 419 and 417). It has no note maturity before mid-2028 and USD 2,940 million of liquidity, including a revolver that was undrawn at every 2026 quarter end. It has scale and spread across four basins, with 433.1 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day in Q3 2026 with the Permian Basin about half of revenue. Operating cash flow after capital spending funds the dividend several times over. The merger was equity-funded, and lenders reaffirmed a borrowing base of USD 5,000 million after the quarter.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Net debt reduction between 2026-03-31 and 2026-09-30 = 7,353 - 6,014 = 1,339. 2. Notes assumed from Civitas and still outstanding = 456 (8.375 percent) + 1,000 (8.625 percent) + 1,350 (8.75 percent) + 750 (9.625 percent) = 3,556. Annual coupons = 38.2 + 86.3 + 118.1 + 72.2 = 314.8 (from 456 x 8.375 percent = 38.19, 1,000 x 8.625 percent = 86.25, 1,350 x 8.75 percent = 118.125, 750 x 9.625 percent = 72.1875, sum 314.75). Weighted coupon = 314.75 / 3,556 = 8.85 percent. 3. Maturities 2028 to 2031 = 856 + 750 + 1,000 + 1,350 = 3,956. Maturities 2032 to 2034 = 750 + 750 + 1,000 = 2,500. Total = 6,456, equal to principal. 4. Cash after dividends and repurchases, nine months 2026 = operating cash flow less capital expenditures 845 - dividends paid 187 - cash repurchases of common stock 166 = 492. Inputs from the CP-1 financial table and CP-1A shareholder return rows (Q3 10-Q page:8 for the cash repurchase figure, a pinned-source locator added for the trace). 5. Redemptions at par since March: 400 (2026-05-11) + 419 (2026-06-01) + 417 (2026-09-04) = 1,236, matching the CP-1 cross-check of 924 + 1,236 = 2,160 cash paid to repurchase notes. 6. Leverage and cover figures are those of the CP-1 handoff: 1.42x net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDAX, 1.53x total debt, 12.73x trailing EBITDAX to trailing cash interest, 8.28x trailing EBITDAX to run-rate coupons of 510.1 per year (weighted coupon 7.90 percent).

Weighted coupon = 314.75 / 3,556 = 8.85 percent.

4. Cash after dividends and repurchases, nine months 2026 = operating cash flow less capital expenditures 845 - dividends paid 187 - cash repurchases of common stock 166 = 492. Inputs from the CP-1 financial table and CP-1A shareholder return rows (Q3 10-Q page:8 for the cash repurchase figure, a pinned-source locator added for the trace).
5. Redemptions at par since March: 400 (2026-05-11) + 419 (2026-06-01) + 417 (2026-09-04) = 1,236, matching the CP-1 cross-check of 924 + 1,236 = 2,160 cash paid to repurchase notes.

6. Leverage and cover figures are those of the CP-1 handoff: 1.42x net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDAX, 1.53x total debt, 12.73x trailing EBITDAX to trailing cash interest, 8.28x trailing EBITDAX to run-rate coupons of 510.1 per year (weighted coupon 7.90 percent).

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested snapshot work for SM Energy Co with stated limitations. The financial statements, the debt note, the liquidity table, the merger and divestiture notes, the derivative notes and the non-GAAP reconciliation are all present and located. What the set cannot do is confirm governing legal terms, current covenant levels after the credit agreement was amended, ratings, post-merger reserves, or anything shown only on investor slides. Prior-year columns are the pre-merger company. | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Trailing-period metrics must be labelled as mixing a standalone and a merged period. |

Proceed to CP-1, then CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 in the order CP-OS plans them. No consumer is marked DO NOT RUN: none is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-1 (financial base: normalized statements, debt, liquidity, EBITDAX definition review and credit metrics) for SM Energy Co (issuer id sm, ticker SM; the registrant is SM ENERGY COMPANY with its consolidated subsidiaries), as of 2026-11-05. Pathway credit_snapshot, case kind public, cutoff 2026-11-05. Reporting currency USD; every amount below is US$ millions unless a cell says otherwise. Current period q3-2026 (quarter and nine months ended 2026-09-30); prior period fy-2025 (year ended 2025-12-31). Requested use: the financial base for the credit snapshot report blocks (key findings, financials and credit metrics, chart strip, transaction summary) and for CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5.

Perimeter: one consolidated registrant. Civitas Resources, Inc. was acquired on 2026-01-30 (the Merger), so FY2025 is the standalone SM Energy perimeter, while Q1 2026 contains the acquired business only from 2026-01-30 and Q2 and Q3 2026 contain it in full. The South Texas assets were sold on 2026-04-30. No pro forma statements are supplied beyond the revenue and net income lines in the Q3 10-Q (page:13). The upstream CP-0 readiness handoff is carried forward: current covenant levels, the executed credit agreement and indentures, guarantor lists, ratings and slides are not supplied, and prior-year columns are pre-merger.

## Findings

### Financial base view

The filed financials support a reliable base for September 30, 2026 balance-sheet items and a bounded base for trailing flow metrics. At that date the company reports only fixed-rate unsecured senior notes plus an undrawn secured revolver, with printed principal, carrying value and fair value for every series, and printed cash, commitments and letters of credit. Those balance-sheet items are directly sourced and cross-checked to the management net debt reconciliation. The flow metrics are weaker: FY2025 is the standalone company, Q1 2026 holds two months of the acquired business, and the trailing figures therefore combine unlike perimeters. Trailing leverage and cover below are computed on that mixed basis and are labelled so; they are not pro forma and not the covenant calculation. Current covenant thresholds and definitions are not supplied, so headroom is shown only as an indication against the older FY2025 ceiling.

### Debt schedule at 2026-09-30

Principal, premium and costs are as printed. All Senior Notes are unsecured senior obligations of SM Energy Company, rank equally with each other, and are guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by each existing subsidiary that guarantees the Credit Agreement (Q3 page:21); the guarantor entities are not named in the supplied sources. The revolver is secured: the Credit Agreement requires mortgage liens on at least 85 percent of the total PV-9 of proved properties, and the same collateral secures derivative obligations (Q3 page:26). Maturity profile: no Senior Notes mature before mid-2028 (Q3 page:21); the first maturities are 856 in calendar 2028, so 0 falls due within twelve months of the cutoff. No facility is stated to expire within twelve months of 2026-11-05, but the maturity of revolver commitments that were not elected for extension is not stated (see Gaps).
### Liquidity at 2026-09-30
| Component | Amount | Source and basis |
| Cash and cash equivalents | 442 | Q3 page:5; no restricted cash is shown separately, and the cash flow statement ends at the same 442 |

At 2026-10-22 the revolver table is unchanged (drawn 0, letters of credit 2, availability 2,498); cash at that date is not supplied, so liquidity at 2026-10-22 is not calculable. The semi-annual borrowing base redetermination after the quarter reaffirmed the 5.0 billion borrowing base and the 2.5 billion commitments (Q3 page:17); the next one is scheduled for April 1, 2027.
### EBITDAX and definition review

The company's adjusted EBITDAX starts from net income and adds back interest, tax, depletion, depreciation and amortization, exploration, stock-based compensation, the full mark-to-market on derivatives, transaction and integration costs and the divestiture result, and then deducts net derivative settlement losses (or adds gains). Items that matter for credit comparison:
| Item | Nine months 2026 (US$m) | Consequence |
| Net derivative loss added back | 1,109 | Non-cash mark-to-market; excluded from EBITDAX |
| Net derivative settlement loss deducted | (457) | Realized hedge losses reduce EBITDAX, so the measure is net of cash hedge results |
| Transaction and integration costs added back | 177 | Of which cash 157 per the operating cash reconciliation; EBITDAX is therefore higher than a measure that treats these costs as recurring |
| Gain on divestiture deducted | (260) | Removed from EBITDAX as a non-operating result |
| Net cash provided by operating activities | 2,865 | Operating cash flow was lower than adjusted EBITDAX by the interest, tax, one-time cost and working capital items in the reconciliation |

The covenant uses "total funded debt, as defined in the Credit Agreement" over "adjusted EBITDAX" (Q3 page:60). The company's November release defines net debt as senior notes principal plus revolver drawings less cash and also calls it "total funded debt" (R3 page:11). Whether the covenant nets cash, and whether covenant EBITDAX is pro forma for acquisitions and divestitures, is not stated in the supplied sources. The Fourth Amendment of 2026-01-30 amended the covenant definitions (Q3 page:17), so the definition in force today is not shown. The metrics in this handoff follow the company's reported adjusted EBITDAX, not the covenant definition.

| Test | Level stated | Reported figure | Headroom |

| Total funded debt to 12-month trailing adjusted EBITDAX, last day of each fiscal quarter | Not greater than 3.50 to 1.00 (10-K page:161, as of FY2025, before the Fourth Amendment) | Not supplied: the filings state compliance but print no covenant ratio | Not calculable on current terms. Indication only: the net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDAX ratio computed here is 1.42x against the older 3.50x ceiling, a gap of 2.08 turns, on a basis that may differ from the covenant definition |

| Adjusted current ratio, last day of any fiscal quarter | Not less than 1.00 to 1.00 (10-K page:161, as of FY2025, before the Fourth Amendment) | Not supplied | Not calculable: the Credit Agreement definition of adjusted current ratio is not supplied, so the balance sheet current ratio is not substituted |

Both the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q state compliance with all financial and non-financial covenants as of the balance sheet date and through filing (10-K page:162, Q3 page:21). No step-downs are described in the supplied text. The credit agreement also contains a springing maturity (Third Amendment, October 13, 2025: the maturity of October 1, 2029 can be accelerated if notes maturing within 91 days exceed 50 in aggregate and availability less those notes is under 20 percent of commitments; 10-K page:158). Whether it survives the Fourth Amendment is not stated; with no notes due before mid-2028 it is not close to a trigger on the supplied facts.
### Claims outside the debt figure

| Derivative liabilities, current | 552 at 2026-09-30 (against 2 at 2025-12-31) | No | Q3 page:5 |

### Operating context for the metrics
| Average net daily equivalent production (MBOE per day) | 206.9 | 371.2 | 439.7 | 433.1 |

Average daily production more than doubled between Q4 2025 and Q2 2026, from 206.9 to 439.7 MBOE per day,, which is why year-over-year comparisons in the 10-Q are not like-for-like. One reportable segment exists, so no segment table is extracted (Q3 page:29).
### Cross-checks and source differences

- Net debt of 6,014 equals Senior Notes principal of 6,456 less cash of 442 and matches the release reconciliation (R3 page:14). The 7.4 billion net debt stated for 2026-03-31 in the release (R3 page:1) agrees with 7,353 computed here from Q1 principal of 7,802 and cash of 449.
- Cash paid to repurchase Senior Notes in the nine months (2,160) equals the tender consideration (924) plus the three redemptions at par (400, 419 and 417): 924 plus 1,236 equals 2,160.

- Net proceeds from the 2034 notes are 985 with fees of 15 in the Q1 10-Q (Q1 page:20) and 984 with fees of 16 in the Q3 10-Q (Q3 page:20). The later filing is used; the difference of 1 is unexplained.

- Proceeds of the divestiture: 897 in the Q2 10-Q cash flow statement, 889 in the Q3 10-Q cash flow statement and 888 in the Q3 MD&A text; the final net cash proceeds are 894 including a post-quarter settlement. The filing statement amounts are used for cash flow and 894 for final proceeds.
- Interest expense plus capitalized interest: capitalized interest was 43 in the nine months (Q3 page:21), so total interest incurred before capitalization was higher than the 340 expensed.
- Prior-year columns (Q3 2025 and nine months 2025) are the standalone company with 115 million diluted shares against 239 million in Q3 2026 (Q3 page:6); they are not used in the metrics above.
## Calculations
All inputs are printed in the cited chunks; each derived value shows its formula.

1. Trailing (last twelve months) adjusted EBITDAX = FY2025 - prior-year year-to-date + current-year year-to-date. Q1 2026: 2,255 - 589 + 970 = 2,636. Q2 2026: 2,255 - 1,158 + 2,376 = 3,473. Q3 2026: 2,255 - 1,747 + 3,717 = 4,225. Inputs: 10-K page:131 (2,255); Q1 page:62 (589, 970); Q2 page:62 (1,158, 2,376); Q3 page:60 (1,747, 3,717). Cross-check by summing four discrete quarters at Q3: 509 (Q4 2025, Q1 page:62) + 970 + 1,406 + 1,341 = 4,226, which differs by 1 from 4,225 because the filings round.

2. Trailing cash interest paid, net of capitalized interest = FY2025 - prior-year year-to-date + current year-to-date. Q1 2026: 166 - 82 + 95 = 179. Q2 2026: 166 - 85 + 185 = 266. Q3 2026: 166 - 165 + 331 = 332. Inputs: 10-K page:137; Q1 page:7; Q2 page:8; Q3 page:8. Discrete cash interest: Q2 = 185 - 95 = 90; Q3 = 331 - 185 = 146.

6. Run-rate coupon cross-check at 2026-09-30 principal: 456 x 8.375% + 400 x 6.5% + 750 x 6.75% + 1,000 x 8.625% + 1,350 x 8.75% + 750 x 7.0% + 750 x 9.625% + 1,000 x 6.625% = 38.2 + 26.0 + 50.6 + 86.3 + 118.1 + 52.5 + 72.2 + 66.3 = 510.1 per year, or 7.90 percent of 6,456. Trailing adjusted EBITDAX over this run-rate coupon is 4,225 / 510.1 = 8.28x. This uses coupons, not cash paid, and ignores capitalized interest and premium amortization; it shows that cover on the current debt stack is lower than the 12.73x blended trailing figure.

7. Quarter discrete flows: capital expenditures Q2 = 1,309 - 555 = 754; Q3 = 2,020 - 1,309 = 711. Dividends paid Q2 = 135 - 82 = 53; Q3 = 187 - 135 = 52. Cash repurchases of common stock Q3 = 166 - 87 = 79. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures: FY2025 2,011 - 1,438 = 573; Q1 640 - 555 = 85; Q2 1,103 - 754 = 349; Q3 1,122 - 711 = 411; nine months 2,865 - 2,020 = 845, equal to 85 + 349 + 411. This is not the company adjusted free cash flow, which is before accruals and differs.
8. Liquidity = cash + (commitments - drawn - letters of credit). Q3 2026: 442 + (2,500 - 0 - 2) = 442 + 2,498 = 2,940.

10. Fair value total = 464 + 400 + 753 + 1,035 + 1,397 + 747 + 805 + 970 = 6,571, which exceeds principal of 6,456 by 115 in aggregate; the 2034 notes (970 against 1,000) are priced furthest below principal and the 2032 notes only slightly below (747 against 750); the 2028 (8.375%), 2029, 2030, 2031 and 2033 series (464, 753, 1,035, 1,397, 805) are above principal and the 6.5% notes due 2028 are at principal (400).

11. Net derivative position = (552 + 13) - (93 + 12) = 460 liability at 2026-09-30, equal to 565 less 105 in the fair value table (Q3 page:26). At 2025-12-31 the fair value table shows assets of 89 and liabilities of 4, a net asset of 85.
12. Indicative covenant gap = 3.50 - 1.42 = 2.08 turns; indication only, see Covenants.
## Gaps

Nothing dated after the cutoff 2026-11-05 is used as fact.
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1A. Carry forward: use the 9/30/26 balance-sheet items (principal 6,456, cash 442, availability 2,498, liquidity 2,940, net debt 6,014) as directly sourced; label every trailing flow metric as mixed perimeter and not pro forma; treat the 3.50x and 1.00x covenant levels as FY2025 and pre-amendment; write Not supplied for ratings, guarantors, executed legal terms and slide content; and keep the derivative liability, delivery and drilling commitments outside the debt figure while naming them in the credit synthesis.

spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-1A (business, ownership, transaction and governance context) for SM Energy Co (issuer id sm, ticker SM; registrant SM ENERGY COMPANY), as of 2026-11-05. Pathway credit_snapshot, case kind public, cutoff 2026-11-05, reporting currency USD. Current period q3-2026; prior period fy-2025. Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor? Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change.

Scope limits carried from the upstream handoffs: the sources are the FY2025 10-K, three 2026 10-Qs and three earnings releases. No credit agreement, indentures, proxy statement, ratings or investor slides are supplied. Figures below that also appear in the CP-1 financial handoff are quoted exactly as that handoff states them; CP-1 is not corrected by this module. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given. Material from outside the sources is not used; where a statement is management's, it is labelled Management Language.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
| EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit99108052026er.htm.jsonl | c611381a32ea896857849afba30a25e0af8ac568cabbb54d05c3d2eded519c0a |

Context (user settings, not issuer evidence): context, sha256 816e6f5709a9a2983bc6f7b0c91f473b414f35053a0b72e52f3a0a46de98a561. Locators `page:N` are extraction chunk numbers. "10-K" is the FY2025 annual report; "Q1", "Q2" and "Q3" are the 10-Qs for the quarters ended 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30; "R1", "R2" and "R3" are the May, August and November 2026 earnings releases.
### Handoffs relied on
| Module | sha256 |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| SM Energy is a widely held, oil-weighted US shale producer that expanded to four basins through the January 2026 Civitas merger, then sold assets and redeemed notes to cut debt. No creditor-adverse behaviour is documented. | Medium | Legal documents, ownership detail, ratings and post-merger reserves are not supplied, so legal capacity is untested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The merger was paid in shares, and former Civitas holders own 52 percent of the company; no sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed. | Equity funded the deal, so debt was not raised to buy it; Civitas debt of $4.9 billion principal was assumed. | High |

| Asset sales and cash flow retired notes due 2026 and 2027 and part of a high-coupon 2028 issue, leaving no note maturity until mid-2028. | Refinancing risk is pushed out, and the interest burden on the assumed notes was reduced. | High |

| Revenue is mostly oil, and the Permian Basin supplies about half of production revenue. Hedge prices sit below recent realized oil prices, and the derivative position is a liability. | Cash flow is sensitive to oil prices and basis; hedges cap upside. | High |

| Shareholder returns continue beside debt reduction: dividends and buybacks are paid and a buyback target is set as a share of free cash flow. | Returns compete with deleveraging; no debt-funded distribution is documented. | Medium |
| Reserves, customer concentration and employee data are from before the merger and the asset sale. | The current reserve base and buyer concentration cannot be stated. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

SM Energy is an independent oil and gas producer whose profile changed in one step on 2026-01-30, when it acquired Civitas Resources for stock and became a four-basin operator, then partly reversed the change by selling its southern Maverick Basin assets on 2026-04-30. For a creditor the transaction matters for four reasons. First, it was paid mainly in equity, with no sponsor and no leveraged buyout structure; the debt increase came from assumed notes, not new borrowing, and the revolver was left undrawn. Second, management used asset-sale proceeds and cash flow to retire the shortest notes and part of the highest-coupon assumed issue, so the first note maturity is mid-2028 and revolver availability is intact. Third, the operating base is oil-weighted and exposed to price, basis and takeaway constraints, partly offset by a hedge book priced below recent realized oil prices that shows as a liability. Fourth, the evidence on ownership control, legal capacity under the indentures and reserves after the merger is missing, so conclusions about willingness are supported by documented actions only, and conclusions about permissions are not drawn. The documented behaviour is deleveraging with continuing shareholder returns; no priming, uptiering, drop-down, debt-funded distribution or related-party leakage appears in the supplied text.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Evidence (locator and exact quote) | Risk mechanic and credit implication |

| Business | Independent energy company engaged in acquiring, exploring, developing and producing oil, gas and NGLs; all operations are in the United States | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 "We are an independent energy company engaged in the acquisition, exploration, development, and production of oil, gas, and NGLs"; 10-K page:17 "All of our operations are conducted in the United States" | Commodity price taker with one reportable segment (Q3 page:29), so revenue is a direct function of volume and realized price; no diversification outside the sector |

| Footprint after the merger | Four operating areas: Permian Basin (Midland and Delaware), DJ Basin, South Texas and Uinta Basin; approximate net acres 230,000, 300,000, 95,000 and 99,000 | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:34 "Our oil-weighted, liquids-rich asset base spans four operating areas within the United States" | Scale and basin spread raise resilience to a single-basin event but add integration and basin-specific constraints |

| Revenue streams | Oil, gas and NGL production revenue; midstream operations acquired in the merger are ancillary to the single segment | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:29 "Midstream operations acquired in the Merger are considered ancillary to, and are managed as part of, the E&P Segment" | No separate fee-based earnings stream; cash flow depends on commodity prices |

| Revenue mix, Q3 2026 | Oil revenue 1,816 of production revenue 2,160; Permian 51 percent, DJ Basin 27 percent, Uinta Basin 13 percent, South Texas 9 percent | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:14 "Oil production revenue" table and "Relative percentage of total Oil, Gas, and NGL production revenue" | Oil share about 84 percent (derived, see Calculations) makes revenue most sensitive to the crude price; basin concentration in the Permian is the largest single driver |

| Production | Q3 2026 average 433.1 MBOE per day: Permian 222.7, DJ Basin 119.4, South Texas 46.3, Uinta Basin 44.7 | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:38 "Average net daily equivalent production decreased sequentially by five percent to 222.7 MBOE per day" | Volume is slightly lower than Q2 (439.7); Permian fell sequentially by five percent |

| Volume risks | Permian downtime for compliance and safety work on acquired assets and temporary shut-ins, and Uinta takeaway constraints expected to be resolved in early 2027; full-year oil guidance lowered by one percent to 220-222 MBbl per day | Management Language | R3 page:2 "We also experienced approximately 4 MBbl/d of takeaway constraints in the Uinta Basin" | Near-term oil volume shortfall reduces cash conversion; resolution timing is management's expectation, not documented fact |

| Pricing | Realized Q3 oil 85.76 per Bbl against NYMEX 85.79; gas realized 2.48 per Mcf against NYMEX 2.95; NGL 29.40 against OPIS 31.64; Q2 gas realized 0.17 per Mcf | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:40 "Realized price (per Mcf) $ 2.48 $ 0.17 $ 2.19"; Q3 page:35 "Regional basis differentials in the Permian Basin and the DJ Basin have adversely impacted our realized gas prices" | Gas and NGL realizations sit below benchmarks, and Q2 shows how a basis blow-out can almost remove gas revenue; oil is realized near benchmark |

| Hedging | Swaps, collars and basis swaps through Q2 2028; Q4 2026 oil swaps 7,673 MBbl at 61.22 and collars 3,289 MBbl with a 58.66 floor; net fair value a liability of 460 at 2026-09-30 | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:24 "The fair value of commodity derivative contracts at September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, was a net liability of $460 million and a net asset of $85 million" | Hedge prices are below the Q3 realized oil price, so settlements are a cash cost now; hedges protect downside but cap upside and put mark-to-market stress on earnings; derivatives share collateral with the revolver (Q3 page:26) |

| Cost structure | Q3 2026 per BOE: lease operating expense 7.02, transportation 3.53, DD&A 14.81, G&A 1.40; production taxes 6.4 percent of production revenue | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:42 "Lease operating expense (per BOE) $ 7.02 $ 6.71 $ 6.25 $ 5.55" | Lease operating expense per BOE rose each quarter since Q4 2025 (5.55 to 7.02), which squeezes margin if prices fall; G&A fell as one-time integration costs faded |

| Capital spending | 2026 capital program about 2.75 billion before acquisitions; Q4 2026 about 610; funded from operating cash flow with the revolver as backup | Management Language | R3 page:3 "Capital Expenditures2 ~$610 ~$2,750" | Capital flexibility exists (rig counts are set per basin, Q3 page:38), but guidance is not a contract |

| Working capital | Accrued production revenue in receivables 791 at 2026-09-30 (193 at 2025-12-31); accounts payable and accrued expenses are large after the merger | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:14 "Accrued oil, gas, and NGL production revenue included in accounts receivable" | Receivable collection is 30 to 90 days with minimal bad debts (10-K page:138); payables composition is not detailed |

| Customers | FY2025 standalone: one customer 28 percent of production revenue, another 6 percent, a group under common control 12 percent; company says loss of a single purchaser would not materially affect results | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:139 "Major customer #1 $ 931 28 %" | Concentration is pre-merger; the post-merger customer mix is Insufficient Information |

| Reserves | Proved reserves 673.0 MMBOE at 2025-12-31, 61 percent proved developed, reserve life index 8.9 years, South Texas 52 percent of reserves; audited by an independent firm for at least 80 percent of PV-10 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:15 "Our total estimated net proved reserves decreased slightly to 673.0 MMBOE"; 10-K page:123 "audit a minimum of 80 percent of our total calculated proved reserve PV-10" | Pre-merger and pre-sale; the reserves sold with 61,000 net acres and those added by Civitas are not stated, so asset coverage and borrowing base support cannot be tested (Insufficient Information) |

| Borrowing base | Borrowing base 5.0 billion against commitments of 2.5 billion, reaffirmed after the quarter | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:17 "reaffirmed both our borrowing base and our aggregate lender commitments at existing levels" | Lenders re-underwrote the reserve base twice in 2026; availability is capped by commitments, not by the base |

| Headcount | 1,241 full-time employees at 2026-02-02, including former Civitas employees | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:32 "we had 1,241 full-time employees" | Single-date figure; not updated after integration savings |
### Company profile
| Field | Value | Category | Locator |
| Issuer and registrant | SM Energy Company with its consolidated subsidiaries; no separate borrower or parent is named in the context | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13; context |
| Country | United States (Delaware corporation; offices in Denver, Colorado; operations in Texas, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah) | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13; Q3 page:9 |
| Sector | Crude petroleum and natural gas exploration and production (context sector: Crude Petroleum & Natural Gas); one reportable segment | Documentary Fact | Context; Q3 page:29 |
| History | Founded in 1908, incorporated in Delaware in 1915, initial public offering in 1992 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 "SM Energy was founded in 1908, incorporated in Delaware in 1915" |

| Listing and ownership class | Listed common equity on the New York Stock Exchange under SM; 235,019,304 shares outstanding at 2026-10-22; no sponsor, controlling holder or holder above any disclosure threshold is named in the supplied sources | Documentary Fact; holder detail Insufficient Information | Q3 page:1; context sponsor blank |

| Control rights and economic interest | Single class of common stock; the Civitas exchange issued 124 million shares, 52 percent of the shares outstanding right after closing | Documentary Fact | Q3 page:33 "representing 52 percent of the shares of SM Energy’s common stock outstanding immediately following the closing of the Merger" |

| Prior ownership and dividend recapitalisation history | No dividend recapitalisation, sponsor ownership history or related-party transaction appears in the supplied sources; the proxy statement is not supplied, so the absence is not confirmed | Insufficient Information | Searched all seven sources |

| Governance | Board committees named include the Governance and Sustainability Committee and the Operations and Environmental, Health and Safety Committee; executive pay in part tied to company-wide financial, operational, environmental and safety measures | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:14; Q3 page:32 |
| Auditor | Ernst & Young LLP, auditor since 2012; reserves audited by Ryder Scott | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:134 "We have served as the Company’s auditor since 2012" |
| Fiscal year and reporting basis | Year ends December 31; GAAP; unaudited interim statements | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:1; Q3 page:9 |

| Credit ratings | Two agencies upgraded the company after the merger citing size, scale, diversification and free cash flow; agency names and rating levels are not supplied | Documentary Fact; levels Insufficient Information | Q3 page:51 "Two major credit rating agencies upgraded our credit ratings following the close of the Merger" |
| Financial position (reference to CP-1) | Senior Notes principal 6,456, cash 442, net debt 6,014 and liquidity 2,940 at 2026-09-30 | Documentary Fact | CP-1 handoff; Q3 pages:5, 19 |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On 2025-11-02 SM Energy signed a merger agreement with Civitas Resources, Inc. (10-K page:14). Stockholders approved the share issuance on 2026-01-27 and the merger closed on 2026-01-30 (Q3 page:33). Each Civitas share was converted into 1.45 SM Energy shares; 124 million shares were issued, equal to 52 percent of the enlarged share count, valued at 2.4 billion on the closing price. The purchase accounting (preliminary) shows equity consideration of 2,409, replacement awards of 29, cash of 226 and total consideration of 2,664 (Q3 page:11); the cash included 201 to repay the Civitas revolver, which released its liens, and 25 for an employee retention program (Q3 page:12). SM Energy is the accounting acquirer, the deal was a tax-free reorganization, and 18 of transaction costs were expensed in the nine months (Q3 page:10). The company assumed 4.9 billion principal of Civitas unsecured senior notes (Q3 page:18); the purchase price allocation lists senior notes assumed at a fair value of 5,090 (Q3 page:11). The Fourth Amendment to the credit agreement, signed at closing, added the Civitas subsidiaries as guarantors, extended the maturity of elected commitments to 2031-01-30, raised commitments from 2.0 billion to 2.5 billion and the borrowing base from 3.0 billion to 5.0 billion, and amended financial covenant definitions (Q3 page:17). Management reports that it actioned about 400 million of run-rate synergies against an original 200 million target (R3 page:1); this is Management Language and no synergy realization in the cash flow statement is supplied.

The divestiture and the debt actions that followed form the second leg. On 2026-02-17 SM Energy agreed to sell about 61,000 net acres in its southern Maverick Basin for 950 million of cash, with a deposit of 7.5 percent placed in escrow (10-K page:183). The sale closed on 2026-04-30 and, after a post-quarter settlement, total net cash proceeds were 894 with a gain of 260 (Q3 page:13). New debt issued in 2026: 1.0 billion of 6.625 percent Senior Notes due 2034, issued at par on 2026-03-09, with net proceeds of 984 after fees (Q3 page:20), used to fund a tender offer. The tender repurchased 894 principal of the 8.375 percent notes due 2028, at 103.175 percent of principal, for total consideration of 924, leaving 456 outstanding (Q3 page:20). Proceeds of the sale redeemed at par the 400 of 5.0 percent notes due 2026 on 2026-05-11 and the 419 of 6.75 percent notes due 2026 on 2026-06-01, and cash flow redeemed the 417 of 6.625 percent notes due 2027 on 2026-09-04 (Q3 pages:20-21). There was no new issuance after the 2034 notes in the supplied sources, and the revolver was undrawn at each quarter end. Net debt fell from 7,353 at 2026-03-31 to 6,014 at 2026-09-30 as stated in the CP-1 handoff, and management says it is on track for low one-times leverage at mid-cycle prices by year-end 2026 (R3 page:2, Management Language; the term is not defined in the sources).

Use of proceeds, liquidity effect and status are all documented for the 2034 notes, tender and redemptions. For the merger itself, no sponsor, bridge financing or new committed financing is described; the revolver was amended, not drawn. No transaction announced but not yet closed appears in the sources as of the cutoff.

1. Revenue durability and margin risk. Evidence: oil is the dominant revenue line (Q3 page:14) and gas realizations fell to 0.17 per Mcf in Q2 on regional differentials (Q3 page:40). Mechanic: price-taking producer with partial hedges; swap and collar floors are below Q3 realized oil prices, so settlements reduce cash now, while the hedge book still limits downside. Implication: cash flow and leverage move with oil and basis; a fall in prices would be cushioned for 2026 and 2027 by hedge volumes (Q3 page:24), but the volumes against 2027 production are not determinable because 2027 production guidance is not supplied. 3. Refinancing and maturity. Evidence: no notes mature until mid-2028 (Q3 page:21). 4. Sponsor alignment and distributions. Evidence: widely held listed equity, no sponsor, equity-paid deal. Mechanic: shareholder returns are funded from free cash flow beside debt reduction. Implication: no extraction pattern is documented; the monitoring point is the pace of buybacks against leverage targets, because management states returns are evaluated "in the context of our leverage trajectory" (Q3 page:64).

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for SM Energy Co as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway, reporting currency USD. It combines the financial base and the business and transaction context built earlier in this run from the FY2025 10-K, the three 2026 10-Qs and the three 2026 earnings releases. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
| EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit99108052026er.htm.jsonl | c611381a32ea896857849afba30a25e0af8ac568cabbb54d05c3d2eded519c0a |

Context (user settings, not issuer evidence): context, sha256 816e6f5709a9a2983bc6f7b0c91f473b414f35053a0b72e52f3a0a46de98a561. This module works from the upstream handoffs, not from source text; where a source locator appears below it points to a pinned source only to help the evidence trace and is flagged as such.
### Handoffs relied on
| Module | sha256 |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| SM Energy is financially sound and improving: net debt is USD 6,014 million, leverage is 1.42x, liquidity is USD 2,940 million and no note matures before mid-2028. It remains an oil-price story. | Medium | Trailing earnings mix the old and merged company, and covenant terms, ratings and legal documents are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt fell from USD 7,353 million after the first quarter to USD 6,014 million after the third, funded by the asset sale and operating cash flow. | Leverage fell from 2.79x to 1.42x on the filed trailing basis without drawing the revolver. | Medium |
| Liquidity is USD 2,940 million, and the first note maturity is mid-2028. | Near-term refinancing and liquidity risk is low on the filed numbers. | High |
| Interest cover is 12.73x on a blended trailing basis but 8.28x against run-rate coupons. | The lower figure better reflects the current, higher-cost debt stack. | Medium |

| Revenue is oil-weighted and hedges are priced below recent realized oil prices; the derivative position is a liability of USD 460 million. | Cash flow moves with oil and basis, and hedges cap the upside. | Medium |
| Dividends and buybacks continue beside debt reduction. | Returns compete with deleveraging, but no debt-funded distribution is documented. | Medium |
### Credit view

SM Energy's credit standing is sound and improving, but it depends on oil prices and on a newly merged earnings base. The strongest support is balance-sheet strength: net debt of USD 6,014 million is 1.42x trailing adjusted EBITDAX, the revolver is undrawn, liquidity is USD 2,940 million, and no note matures before mid-2028. The weakest point is that trailing earnings blend the old and merged company, so leverage is not on a clean pro forma basis, and covenant terms, ratings and legal documents are not in the sources. The outcome will be decided by oil prices and basis through 2027, by whether free cash flow keeps funding both debt reduction and shareholder returns, and by how the USD 3,956 million of notes due 2028 to 2031 is managed.
### Key findings

SM Energy cut net debt by USD 1,339 million in two quarters, from USD 7,353 million at 2026-03-31 to USD 6,014 million at 2026-09-30, and trailing leverage fell from 2.79x to 1.42x over the same dates [CP-1: leverage and net debt tables; calculation 3]. The mechanism was asset-sale proceeds of USD 894 million and operating cash flow, which together redeemed the 2026 and 2027 notes at par while the revolver stayed undrawn at each quarter end [CP-1A: transaction summary]. The ratio improved partly because trailing earnings gradually absorbed more of the acquired business, so some of the decline is a perimeter effect and not debt repayment alone. The Civitas merger closed on 2026-01-30 and was equity-funded, so SM Energy's creditors face a larger company with the same unsecured senior notes and a secured revolver, not a leveraged buyout.

Liquidity is strong: cash of USD 442 million plus USD 2,498 million of undrawn revolver capacity gives USD 2,940 million, while the borrowing base of USD 5,000 million is twice the USD 2,500 million of commitments, so availability is capped by lender commitments, not by reserves [CP-1: liquidity]. The maturity ladder is USD 856 million in 2028, USD 750 million in 2029, USD 1,000 million in 2030, USD 1,350 million in 2031 and USD 2,500 million across 2032 to 2034, so the wall begins in mid-2028 and totals USD 3,956 million across 2028 to 2031 [CP-1: debt maturities]. Cash generation covers the dividends: operating cash flow less capital expenditures was USD 845 million in the nine months against USD 187 million of dividends and USD 166 million of share repurchases, leaving USD 492 million before asset-sale proceeds [CP-1: calculation 7; this module's calculation 4].

The cost of the debt stack is the main structural concern. The notes carry a weighted coupon of 7.90 percent, or USD 510.1 million of coupons a year, and the notes assumed from Civitas, USD 3,556 million at 8.375 to 9.625 percent, are the most expensive layer, with a weighted coupon of 8.85 percent [CP-1: debt schedule; calculation 2]. Trailing cash interest cover of 12.73x blends the lighter pre-merger interest burden with the post-merger burden; against run-rate coupons the cover is 8.28x, which is the better guide to the current stack. Whether the high-coupon notes can be called or refinanced early depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

Earnings carry commodity risk. Oil was about 84 percent of Q3 2026 production revenue and the Permian Basin about half of it [CP-1A: company and operating model]. Hedges are swaps and collars through the second quarter of 2028 with prices below recent realized oil prices, so they cost cash now and cap upside, and the net derivative position is a liability of USD 460 million [CP-1A: hedging]. Operating issues also matter: oil production guidance was cut for Permian downtime on acquired assets and Uinta takeaway constraints, and lease operating cost per barrel of oil equivalent has risen every quarter since Q4 2025 [CP-1A: volume risks, cost structure]. Claims outside the debt figure include delivery commitments with up to USD 205 million of deficiency payments if nothing were delivered, liquidated damages of up to USD 64 million under a drilling agreement, and a drilling commitment management expects to be excused [CP-1: claims outside the debt figure].

Shareholder returns and governance show no creditor-adverse behaviour in the documents: the merger was paid in shares, there is no sponsor, and no debt-funded distribution, drop-down or priming appears [CP-1A: behaviour table]. Management targets about 20 percent of free cash flow after dividends for repurchases, which competes with deleveraging, though management says its leverage trajectory is part of that allocation. Legal capacity to distribute cash or add priority debt cannot be tested because the indentures and the credit agreement are not supplied.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. SM Energy has low net leverage of 1.42x on the filed trailing basis and has shown it will use asset sales and cash flow to retire debt, with USD 1,236 million of notes redeemed at par since March from sale proceeds and cash flow (400, 419 and 417). It has no note maturity before mid-2028 and USD 2,940 million of liquidity, including a revolver that was undrawn at every 2026 quarter end. It has scale and spread across four basins, with 433.1 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day in Q3 2026 with the Permian Basin about half of revenue. Operating cash flow after capital spending funds the dividend several times over. The merger was equity-funded, and lenders reaffirmed a borrowing base of USD 5,000 million after the quarter.

Weaknesses. SM Energy remains a price taker with revenue about 84 percent oil, hedges below recent realized prices and a net derivative liability of USD 460 million. Its trailing credit metrics mix standalone and merged periods and are not covenant metrics. Interest cost is higher after the merger, as the assumed notes carry coupons of 8.375 to 9.625 percent and will keep interest above the pre-merger run-rate until they are retired or refinanced. Integration and operating execution still carry risk, with oil guidance lowered, rising unit lease operating costs and acquired-asset downtime. Off-debt commitments exist but are unquantified in part. Shareholder returns continue alongside deleveraging. The documentation behind the credit, including covenants, guarantors, indentures, ratings and a post-merger reserve base, is not in the sources.
### Credit assessment and thesis
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Fundamental credit view is solid and improving: low trailing net leverage, large undrawn liquidity and no near-term maturities, set against oil-price sensitivity and an earnings base that mixes pre-merger and merged periods | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and maturity tables; CP-1A revenue mix, hedging, transaction summary and behaviour rows |

| Thesis | SM Energy is using asset sales and operating cash flow to deleverage a larger, oil-weighted, equity-funded merged company, and the credit is decided by oil prices and by managing the 2028 to 2031 maturities | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 net debt movement and maturities; CP-1A operating model |

Confidence is Medium, not High, because the upstream business handoff rates readiness for this module as ready with limitations, not ready: ownership detail, legal documents, ratings and the post-merger reserve base are missing.
### Strengths and weaknesses register
| Type | Label | Category | Basis |
| Strength | Low trailing net leverage of 1.42x | Documentary Fact (figure); trailing basis is Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 leverage table |
| Strength | Liquidity of USD 2,940 million, revolver undrawn | Documentary Fact | CP-1 liquidity table |
| Strength | No note maturity before mid-2028 | Documentary Fact | CP-1 debt maturities |
| Strength | Diversified four-basin base, Permian about half of revenue | Documentary Fact | CP-1A company and operating model |
| Strength | Equity-funded merger, no sponsor, no documented creditor-adverse action | Documentary Fact; absence of adverse action is Analyst Interpretation | CP-1A behaviour table |
| Strength | Borrowing base of USD 5,000 million reaffirmed | Documentary Fact | CP-1A operating model; CP-1 liquidity |
| Weakness | Oil-weighted revenue, hedges below recent realized prices, net derivative liability of USD 460 million | Documentary Fact | CP-1A hedging; CP-1 claims outside debt |
| Weakness | Trailing metrics mix perimeters | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 chart notes |
| Weakness | High-coupon assumed notes and cover of 8.28x on run-rate coupons | Documentary Fact (coupons); cover is Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 debt schedule and calculations |

| Weakness | Operating execution: lowered oil guidance, acquired-asset downtime, rising lease operating cost | Management Language (guidance and causes); trend is Documentary Fact | CP-1A volume risks and cost structure |
| Weakness | Off-debt commitments, partly unquantified | Documentary Fact | CP-1 claims outside debt |
| Weakness | Covenant terms, indentures, ratings, reserves after the merger not supplied | Insufficient Information | CP-0 and CP-1 gaps |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Oil price and basis | Revenue is mostly oil and gas realizations fell to USD 0.17 per Mcf in Q2 on regional differentials; hedges cover part of volumes at prices below recent realized levels | Cash flow, leverage and the capacity to keep returning cash fall together in a price decline; hedges soften but do not remove this | Material |

| Merged earnings base and integration | Trailing EBITDAX includes the acquired business for part of the period; oil guidance cut for downtime and takeaway limits | Leverage and cover on a pro forma basis are unknown; execution slippage would slow deleveraging | Material |

| Refinancing and cost of assumed notes | Notes assumed at 8.375 to 9.625 percent are the most expensive layer, and call terms are not supplied | Interest burden stays high until refinanced; maturity wall of USD 3,956 million from 2028 to 2031 | Material |

| Reserve base after the merger and sale | Only pre-merger reserves are supplied; the reserves sold with the South Texas assets are not stated | Asset coverage and borrowing base support cannot be tested | Material |
| Covenants and legal capacity | Financial covenant definitions were amended in January 2026 and indentures are not supplied | Headroom and permitted distributions cannot be verified | Material |
| Shareholder returns versus deleveraging | Repurchase target tied to free cash flow after dividends | Slower deleveraging if returns rise; no debt-funded distribution documented | Minor |

| Off-debt claims | Derivative liability, delivery deficiency exposure, drilling commitments | Claims ranking outside debt could draw on cash in a downturn; delivery and drilling items are conditional | Minor |
## Calculations
All inputs come from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs; amounts in USD millions.

2. Notes assumed from Civitas and still outstanding = 456 (8.375 percent) + 1,000 (8.625 percent) + 1,350 (8.75 percent) + 750 (9.625 percent) = 3,556. Annual coupons = 38.2 + 86.3 + 118.1 + 72.2 = 314.8 (from 456 x 8.375 percent = 38.19, 1,000 x 8.625 percent = 86.25, 1,350 x 8.75 percent = 118.125, 750 x 9.625 percent = 72.1875, sum 314.75). Weighted coupon = 314.75 / 3,556 = 8.85 percent.

4. Cash after dividends and repurchases, nine months 2026 = operating cash flow less capital expenditures 845 - dividends paid 187 - cash repurchases of common stock 166 = 492. Inputs from the CP-1 financial table and CP-1A shareholder return rows (Q3 10-Q page:8 for the cash repurchase figure, a pinned-source locator added for the trace).
5. Redemptions at par since March: 400 (2026-05-11) + 419 (2026-06-01) + 417 (2026-09-04) = 1,236, matching the CP-1 cross-check of 924 + 1,236 = 2,160 cash paid to repurchase notes.

6. Leverage and cover figures are those of the CP-1 handoff: 1.42x net debt to trailing adjusted EBITDAX, 1.53x total debt, 12.73x trailing EBITDAX to trailing cash interest, 8.28x trailing EBITDAX to run-rate coupons of 510.1 per year (weighted coupon 7.90 percent).
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Pro forma trailing EBITDAX including the acquired business and excluding the divested assets | Leverage and cover on a like-for-like basis cannot be stated; ratios may be overstated or understated | Credit assessment, leverage risk | Material | Obtain pro forma or covenant EBITDAX |

| Current covenant levels, definitions and reported ratios | Headroom is Not calculable; the FY2025 levels pre-date an amendment | Liquidity and default-risk conclusions | Material | Obtain the amended credit agreement or compliance certificate |

| Executed credit agreement and indentures, guarantor lists, call schedules | Legal capacity for distributions and priming, and early refinancing of high-coupon notes, cannot be assessed | Governance and refinancing risk | Material | Obtain documents |
| Ratings and agency names | Rating context and trigger effects not available | Assessment | Minor | Obtain rating reports |

| Ownership above disclosure thresholds, proxy statement | Control and alignment cannot be assessed beyond the equity-funded structure | Sponsor alignment | Minor | Obtain proxy statement |

| Price sensitivity is not in the upstream handoffs; the Q3 10-Q (page:58) discloses the effect of a ten percent change in realized prices and the offsetting derivative settlements, which the next evidence action can use | The size of the earnings and cash flow exposure to price is unquantified here | Business and financial risk | Material | Quantify from the pinned source in the next module |
| Preliminary purchase price allocation | Acquired asset and liability values may change | Balance sheet analysis | Minor | Use as filed, label preliminary |
| Investor slides referenced in the releases | Management claims beyond release text unverified | Management Language | Minor | Obtain decks |

Inherited limitations: the business handoff is ready for this module with limitations (not ready), which keeps confidence below High; the financial handoff restricts trailing metrics as mixed perimeter; and the readiness handoff withholds legal terms, ratings and slides. SM Energy's analysis is traceable: every material claim in the readiness, financial, business and synthesis handoffs rests on a located passage of a pinned source or on arithmetic that reproduces from such passages, and the handoffs tell one consistent story.
